The shaded square is located in row 4 column 5, namely r4c5. Reasoning: The rule requires that any two squares adjacent by sharing an edge or sharing a corner cannot have the same letter. Therefore the four squares in any 2×2 small square are pairwise adjacent, and the available letters are exactly the four P,Q,R,S, so every 2×2 small square must contain exactly P,Q,R,S. The upper-left 2×2 is already P,Q,R,S. Use r3c3=Q to continue propagating: in the 2×2 of r2-r3, c1-c2, r2c1=R, r2c2=S, and r3c2 is adjacent to r3c3=Q, so r3c2 cannot be Q and can only be P, hence r3c1=Q. Then look at the 2×2 of r2-r3, c2-c3: r2c2=S, r3c2=P, r3c3=Q are already present, so r2c3=R. Next, in the 2×2 of r1-r2, c2-c3, Q,S,R are already present, so r1c3=P. Continue to the right: r1-r2, c3-c4 and r2-r3, c3-c4 together force r1c4=Q, r2c4=S, r3c4=P. Then look at the adjacent 2×2s of c4-c5; it can be obtained that r1c5=P, r2c5=R, r3c5=Q. The shaded square r4c5 is edge-adjacent to r3c5=Q and also corner-adjacent to r3c4=P, so it cannot be Q and also cannot be P. Therefore the only candidates left are R or S. Verify that both are feasible: if row 4 takes R,S,R,S,R, then together with r5c1=Q, row 5 can be taken as Q,P,Q,P,Q, and all 2×2 small squares contain P,Q,R,S. If row 4 takes S,R,S,R,S, row 5 can likewise be taken as Q,P,Q,P,Q, also satisfying all adjacency restrictions. Therefore the shaded square can be either R or S, and cannot be P or Q.

method.method_draft: Label the 5 by 5 grid by rows and columns, with the shaded cell at row 4, column 5. From the image read the given entries: r1c1=P, r1c2=Q, r2c1=R, r2c2=S, r3c3=Q, and r5c1=Q. Use the text rule that edge- or corner-adjacent cells cannot match. Since all four cells of any 2 by 2 block are mutually adjacent and only four letters are available, every 2 by 2 block must contain exactly P,Q,R,S. Propagate this rule from the fixed top-left 2 by 2 block across the first three rows: the constraints force r1c3=P, r2c3=R, r3c2=P, then r1c4=Q, r2c4=S, r3c4=P, and finally r1c5=P, r2c5=R, r3c5=Q. Thus the shaded r4c5 is adjacent to r3c4=P and r3c5=Q, so it cannot be P or Q. To verify both remaining letters are possible, complete row 4 as either R,S,R,S,R or S,R,S,R,S; with r5c1=Q, both force row 5 as Q,P,Q,P,Q and satisfy all 2 by 2 blocks. Therefore the shaded square can be R or S only.

图像描述：图中是一个 5×5 方格。按从上到下为第 1 至第 5 行、从左到右为第 1 至第 5 列标号，已给出的字母为：r1c1=P，r1c2=Q，r2c1=R，r2c2=S，r3c3=Q，r5c1=Q。阴影格位于第 4 行第 5 列，即 r4c5。

推理：规则要求凡是共边或共角相邻的两个格子不能有相同字母。因此任意一个 2×2 小方块中的四个格子两两相邻，而可用字母正好是 P,Q,R,S 四个，所以每个 2×2 小方块必须恰好包含 P,Q,R,S。

左上角 2×2 已经是 P,Q,R,S。利用 r3c3=Q 继续传播：在 r2-r3、c1-c2 的 2×2 中，r2c1=R、r2c2=S，且 r3c2 与 r3c3=Q 相邻，所以 r3c2 不能是 Q，只能为 P，于是 r3c1=Q。再看 r2-r3、c2-c3 的 2×2，已有 r2c2=S、r3c2=P、r3c3=Q，所以 r2c3=R。接着 r1-r2、c2-c3 的 2×2 中已有 Q,S,R，所以 r1c3=P。

继续向右：r1-r2、c3-c4 与 r2-r3、c3-c4 共同迫使 r1c4=Q，r2c4=S，r3c4=P。再看 c4-c5 的相邻 2×2，可得 r1c5=P，r2c5=R，r3c5=Q。

阴影格 r4c5 与 r3c5=Q 共边相邻，也与 r3c4=P 共角相邻，所以它不能是 Q，也不能是 P。因此候选只剩 R 或 S。

验证二者都可行：若第 4 行取 R,S,R,S,R，则结合 r5c1=Q 可取第 5 行为 Q,P,Q,P,Q，所有 2×2 小方块都含 P,Q,R,S。若第 4 行取 S,R,S,R,S，同样可取第 5 行为 Q,P,Q,P,Q，也满足全部相邻限制。因此阴影格既可以是 R，也可以是 S，不能是 P 或 Q。
